concepts: deliberate actions to create a magnetic experience
sections.description: This section grounds Bliss's message in Zara as the illustrated example. It references an annual 'mafia meeting' where a large number of products are cut despite customer affinity, framing pruning as a deliberate strategic move. It notes Zara’s ability to break even in a new store within roughly three months, and highlights the high level of customer engagement (average 17 store visits per year) driven by deliberate actions that shape a continuous product and service experience. The paragraph concludes with a emphasis on knowing customers’ lives to serve them, and the importance of direct, personal engagement in business.
sections.title: Zara case study: assortment pruning and customer experience

summary: In this excerpt from Jeanne Bliss’s talk, Zara is presented as a concrete example of how beloved, prosperous companies sustain magnetic momentum through deliberate business actions. The speaker notes that top brands prune their product lines aggressively (even cutting a hundred products annually) to focus on what customers truly love, while still creating a compelling offer. Zara is highlighted for its ability to break even in a new store within about three months, and for driving high customer touchpoints—visits averaging 17 per year—through a deliberate store and product experience. The overall message emphasizes knowing customers’ lives to serve them effectively, maintaining a continuous, lifecycle-aware product and service experience, and engaging with customers personally in business relationships.
title: Zara as a Case Study in Jeanne Bliss's Talk on Beloved and Prosperous Companies
